output.plainSummary: The synthetic demo model suggests fabric is very likely to ignite if exposed to an ignition source; this is not the chance of a cabin fire occurring. Synthetic fabric tests covered air close to this cabin condition, but the supplied records do not confirm a test at this exact combination [saffire-i]. These are generated demonstration results, not NASA findings.
output.summary: For the proposed microgravity cabin, the model trained on synthetic runs predicts 82% ignition probability and assigns a very-high relative risk band, not a certified safety limit or an operational fire probability. The synthetic dataset's surrounding fabric grid contains 31 runs, with 27 ignitions, but spans a range of oxygen concentrations and pressures rather than only the exact proposed condition. The coverage check reports no gap, so the condition is within reported coverage, although an exact material-and-condition match is not established. Nearby synthetic runs give an estimated flame spread of 1.38 mm/s, with a neighboring-run range of 0.51–2.19 mm/s; that range is not a prediction confidence interval.
riskDrivers: Earth-reference air does not establish fire safety: synthetic fabric runs near the proposed oxygen, pressure and airflow conditions frequently ignited [saffire-i].

The proposed ventilation falls within a flow regime where synthetic BASS and BASS-II ignited runs self-extinguished less often than under lower-flow conditions; ventilation should not be assumed to extinguish a flame [bass] [bass-ii].

Fabric identity matters. Synthetic BASS-II results show different spread behavior for Nomex and cotton-fiberglass fabric, so the generic Fabric label cannot establish the response of the installed material [bass-ii].

relevantEvidence.evidence: In the synthetic dataset, cotton-fiberglass fabric ignited in 21 of 24 runs. Sustained flames spread at a mean of 1.56 mm/s.
relevantEvidence.relevance: Its reported microgravity oxygen, pressure and airflow ranges include the proposed condition, and its fuel is fabric. Range overlap does not establish an exact-condition test.

relevantEvidence.evidence: In the synthetic runs, mean spread was 2.74 mm/s for cotton-fiberglass fabric and 1.00 mm/s for Nomex fabric.
relevantEvidence.relevance: Both are fabrics, demonstrating why the cabin's unspecified fabric composition is an important limitation.

relevantEvidence.evidence: In the synthetic runs, all ignited microgravity runs below 5 cm/s self-extinguished, compared with 18% at 5–30 cm/s.
relevantEvidence.relevance: The proposed airflow lies in the latter band. This supports testing ventilation effects, but does not establish that reducing airflow will reliably suppress this cabin material.

relevantEvidence.evidence: The synthetic dataset reports a mean smoke obscuration of 27.2% for cotton-fiberglass fabric.
relevantEvidence.relevance: This supports including smoke measurements in fabric fire tests near the proposed atmosphere. It does not provide detector response times or performance for the installed fabric.

knowledgeGaps: The supplied records do not identify the cabin fabric's composition, treatment, construction or installed configuration.
Coverage is reported, but the grid aggregates nearby oxygen and pressure conditions and does not establish an exact match in fabric, atmosphere and airflow.
The ignition model has no supplied calibration, validation uncertainty or ignition-source specification. Its output cannot establish operational cabin fire probability.
Detector response and suppression effectiveness for this installed fabric and cabin airflow are not provided.

recommendedTests.test: In microgravity, ignition-test the intended flight fabric at the proposed 21% oxygen, 14.7 psi and approximately 20 cm/s airflow, using representative installed construction and documented ignition exposure.
recommendedTests.rationale: Establishes an exact material-and-condition result rather than relying on generic fabric labels and nearby synthetic runs.

recommendedTests.test: At the proposed 21% oxygen and 14.7 psi in microgravity, test the intended flight fabric at approximately 20 cm/s and at airflow below 5 cm/s; measure ignition, spread, extinction and re-ignition.
recommendedTests.rationale: Tests whether airflow reduction is effective for this fabric instead of treating the synthetic low-flow trend as a suppression guarantee.

recommendedTests.test: At the proposed 21% oxygen, 14.7 psi and approximately 20 cm/s airflow in microgravity, burn the intended flight fabric in a representative installation while evaluating smoke detection and the proposed suppression system.
recommendedTests.rationale: Measures detection and suppression performance that the supplied records do not establish.

prevention: Control ignition sources and limit exposed fabric pending material-specific qualification.
Use this synthetic assessment only to prioritize engineering work; retain applicable NASA flammability standards and certified material testing.
detection: Validate smoke transport and detector response with the actual fabric and representative cabin ventilation; the supplied smoke measurements do not establish alarm timing.
suppression: Do not credit ventilation reduction alone as reliable suppression.
Verify extinguishment and resistance to re-ignition for the installed fabric before assigning suppression-system performance.
